Verified: §1t99s0§.as:3262 Light = base*(0.5+0.4*m*0.1), :3265 Balanced = base*(1+0.2*m*0.1), :3270 Heavy/Dual/Reversed flat 1.4. m=0 gives 0.5/1.0/1.4, exactly RR:156's level-1 Shugyosha row; m=10 gives 0.90/1.20/1.40, exactly RR:155's ceiling triple; m=9 gives 0.86/1.18, which reproduces neither. Nine is also not the top rung: skilldata.xml gives skills 1000/1001/1002 exactly ten <level><value> rows 1..10, and npcdata.xml:535 ships elites at <lvl>10</lvl>. RR:155's 'MASTERY-9 CEILING' label falls. CORRECTION 1: the closing line 'Android diverges ... on a 0-100 mastery scale' is WRONG. The android reads the SAME ten-level ladder (EnemyPlayer.as/EnemyElite.as call xml.getMastery(1000/1001/1002)) and gates its own techniques at >= 3 / >= 4 / >= 5 in MCSPlayer.as:3166-3184, byte-for-byte the same thresholds as the web at §1t99s0§.as:3223-3241. The divergence is in the COEFFICIENT (android 0.005/level and Heavy 1.5, web 0.04/level and Heavy 1.4), not in the domain - which is a stronger reason not to port it, not a weaker one. CORRECTION 2: 'The string table settles the cap independently' overstates. strings.json["8131"] sits among achievement lines ('Reach Dan 10.', 'Farming Level 5.') in the ANDROID v0.682 table - an achievement target is a milestone, and under C2 an android string cannot settle a web cap on its own. The web-side proof is the exact numeric fit at m=10; keep that as the argument. LENS 3, SETTLED: LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:54 ([[combat-core/v0717-stance-table]]) says m=9 gives 'the wiki's 0.9/1.2/1.4 rounded, which CONFIRMS the ledger's mastery-9 reading rather than overturning it'. That is the wrong side of the contradiction: 9 is the ninth of ten rungs, so it is not a ceiling at all, and 0.90/1.20 are exact where 0.86/1.18 are only roundable. Six other banked findings (:28-70) already say mastery-10; that one clause should be struck.

HOLDS. citelint's QUOTE_NOT_LOCATED is a FALSE ALARM - I opened the file and both quoted lines are verbatim: :3272 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' and :3274 'return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;', inside §1t4475s0§ whose opener at :3258 is 'minDamage + Math.random() * damageRange'. :3295-3297 zeroes the same meter on the same predicate, and §1t113s0§.as:348-358 prints getString(175)='Critical Hit' plus Snd_criticalDamage at the same full-meter state - so the finding's 'one 0..192 resource drives stance-unlock at 48 and a 1.3x crit at 192' is right, and RR:190 blocker (2)'s instruction to 'read one crit popup' is discharged from source. Note precisely what falls in RR:152-154: the VALUE 1.3 is VINDICATED, not reversed; what dies is its wiki-only basis and the open action item. LENS 3, SETTLED AGAINST A BANKED FINDING: LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:659-661 ([[frames/critical-evade-states-the-focus-gate]]) calls the full bar 'an evade gate, NOT a crit meter'. I opened that exact frame at that exact crop: the card reads '(PASSIVE SKILL) ALLOWS YOU TO EVADE ATTACKS WHILE SLASHING IN THIS STANCE WHEN YOUR FOCUS BAR IS FULL.' It describes an extra passive; it never denies the crit. And the web code carries BOTH on the same predicate - §1t99s0§.as:3383-3388 returns a dodge (Snd_jump, no damage) when reload==maxreload AND the stance's passive is owned, while :3272-3274 applies the x1.3. THE FORMULAS HOLD BUT THE NAMED OVERTURN DOES NOT. Verified at the artifact: :3094 Light reach = base * 1.4 with NO mastery term; :3105 Balanced reach = base * (1 + 0.2*m*0.1); :3116 Heavy reach = base * (0.5 + 0.4*m*0.1) with the hard clamp 'if(§1t4417s0§ < 100) §1t4417s0§ = 100;' at :3117-3120; and the damage switch at :3259-3271 is indeed the mirror (Light scales, Heavy flat 1.4). The '300/200/100 cannot be a ceiling row, the ceiling multipliers are 1.4/1.20/0.90' point is arithmetically right. BUT the ledger sentence the finding names, RR:156, does NOT fall - I read it and it is CORRECT. 'A level-1 Shugyosha does Light x0.5 / Balanced x1.0 / Heavy x1.4 (Heavy is fixed); Heavy's reach also scales x0.5->x0.9' is exactly the m=0 and m=10 evaluation of the two formulas. The finding's objection - "'Heavy's reach also scales x0.5->x0.9' has the wrong low endpoint (m=1 gives 0.54)" - is WRONG: §1t99s0§.as:107, :109 and :111 declare the three mastery fields 'internal var ... :int = 0', so a character who has not bought the mastery skill sits at m=0 and Heavy reach is exactly 0.5*base. LENS 3, INTERNAL TO THIS PACKET: this directly contradicts packet sibling cite-s27b/stance-damage-ceiling-is-mastery-10-not-mastery-9, which says 'mastery 0 gives Light 0.5 / Balanced 1.0 / Heavy 1.4 - exactly RR:156's level-1 Shugyosha row'. Both cannot be true and #3 is the right side; LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:36 ([[combat-core/mastery-caps-at-ten]]) independently confirms the mastery-0 reading. Not refuted overall - the reach recovery is real and the finding's OWN lane_impact names the overturn that does land: RR:190 blocker (1) 'reach cap in stage px per stance' collapses from three measurements to one base slash length. Route it to RR:190, not RR:156, and strike the low-endpoint objection.

verdicts.reason: REFUTED ON ITS CENTRAL SENTENCE. The numbers are right - I re-verified :3050 'return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48;', :249 '8 * 24' = 192, :3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48)', and the Light->Balanced->Heavy->Light cycle at :3064-3079. But the finding then asserts 'the in-combat stance switch costs no Focus and no Chi: it needs the reload meter at 48/192 = 25%', and that is FALSE. §1t99s0§.as:3160-3166, inside §1t3489s0§ (setStance), reads 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§()) { this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48; ... }' - it DEBITS 48 from the very meter it gates on. §1t9948s0§ is isBattle beyond doubt: the android twin setStance (MCSPlayer.as:3019-3105) has the same three guards in the same three places and each reads 'StageManager.isBattle()'. So the debit fires precisely IN combat. And the meter is Focus: the game's own skill card (frame_0013.jpg, my crop) says 'WHEN YOUR FOCUS BAR IS FULL', so §1t4414s0§/reload IS the Focus bar and the switch costs 48 Focus. LENS 3: this contradicts EIGHT upheld findings - LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:262-266 ('setStance charges a flat 48 frames, which a hard lock would have nothing to charge'), :279-281, :540, :644, and :3241 - and packet sibling cite-s27b/focus-meter-numerics, which I uphold and which quotes :3162 correctly. Its lane_impact compounds the error: 'replace the Focus gate with RELOAD_STANCE_THRESHOLD=48' inverts the banked conclusion that the recreation's Focus-gated switch is FAITHFUL, and a port that takes it ships a gate with no debit, i.e. unlimited stance switching once the bar passes 48. Nothing is destroyed by refuting: gate 48, max 192 and the three-stance cycle are banked seven times over at :257-284 and survive in packet siblings #2 and #7. RR:158 itself DOES fall - I proved it on frames myself - but not on this claim's framing.

There is NO separate Focus resource anywhere in the combat classes: grepping §1t99s0§.as and §1t113s0§.as for 'focus' returns only Flash stage keyboard focus (§1t113s0§.as:403, :417, :423, :1126, :1134) and the FOCUS_START/FOCUS_END animation states.

new_findings.text: REBUILD_READINESS.md:159 says 'The *out-of-combat* switch costing Focus IS real; the *in-combat* switch is a recreation divergence'. The web payload says the exact opposite on both halves. §1t99s0§.as:3160-3166 puts the ONLY charge - 'this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48;' - inside 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§())', the battle predicate (the android twin setStance at MCSPlayer.as:3019-3105 carries the same three guards, each spelled 'StageManager.isBattle()'). I enumerated every occurrence of §1t4414s0§ in §1t99s0§.as - :93, :250, :256, :1203, :1205, :1208, :3050, :3060, :3162-:3169, :3272, :3295-:3297, :3302-:3314, :3320-:3325, :3383, :3707, :4890, :4897 - and :3162 is the sole stance-switch debit and the sole one under a battle guard. So OUT of combat a stance switch is FREE, and IN combat it costs 48 Focus. The ledger has the two cases swapped. The isBattle guard itself is banked (LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:279, :644, :3241) but no finding in the corpus names RR:159 or states the out-of-combat half as free - 'RR:159' returns zero hits.
new_findings.ledger_text: The *out-of-combat* switch costing Focus IS real; the *in-combat* switch is a recreation divergence — label it, don't present it as original.

new_findings.text: The 'Critical Evade' skill card that a banked A1 finding read off film has a web-side code twin nobody has cited, and it shows the full-Focus state gating evasion and crit SIMULTANEOUSLY - so the card and the crit multiplier were never in conflict. §1t99s0§.as:3383-3388, inside the hit-resolution override §1t3274s0§ (opens :3328), reads: 'if(this.§1t4465s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§ && (this.stance == §1t12220s0§ && this.§1t4491s0§(§1t120s0§.§1t10173s0§) > 0 || this.stance == §1t12221s0§ && ...§1t10174s0§ > 0 || this.stance == §1t12222s0§ && ...§1t10175s0§ > 0))' then sets §1t3246s0§ = 12, plays 'Snd_jump' and RETURNS TRUE - i.e. the incoming hit is consumed with no damage applied. A second identical branch sits at :3707. Three separate passives, one per core stance, each a skill the player must own (§1t4491s0§(...) > 0 is a skill-level lookup), all keyed on reload == maxreload. Meanwhile :3272-3274 applies the x1.3 crit on the same predicate. LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md contains zero hits for '3383', '10173' or '4491s0'.
new_findings.ledger_text: ⑤ Focus/crit gating rule — *watch the Focus bar fill/consume.*
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core blocker (5) closes with a fuller rule than 'crit at full': a full Focus bar is a two-effect state - x1.3 on your own damage roll unconditionally, PLUS total evasion of an incoming hit if you own that stance's passive (three separate skills, Light/Balanced/Heavy). Also strike the 'an evade gate, NOT a crit meter' clause from LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:660: the code carries both, so that clause is the only false part of an otherwise correct finding.

new_findings.text: The five obfuscated web stance constants are pinned to names by structural alignment with the android's un-obfuscated MCSPlayer, which fixes a pairing that at least one packet finding got backwards. Android MCSPlayer.as:27/:29/:31/:33/:35 declare LIGHT_STANCE=0, BALANCED_STANCE=1, HEAVY_STANCE=2, DUAL_STANCE=3, REVERSED_STANCE=4. Its deductReloadBar at :3240-3263 groups them LIGHT -> slashUsage/2, BALANCED+REVERSED -> slashUsage, HEAVY+DUAL -> slashUsage*1.5. The web twin §1t4478s0§ at §1t99s0§.as:3293-3316 groups §1t12220s0§ -> /2, §1t12221s0§+§1t12224s0§ -> x1, §1t12222s0§+§1t12223s0§ -> x1.5. The only assignment consistent with both is §1t12220s0§=LIGHT, §1t12221s0§=BALANCED, §1t12222s0§=HEAVY, §1t12223s0§=DUAL, §1t12224s0§=REVERSED, and the setStance reach switch corroborates it independently: web :3130-3140 (§1t12224s0§, base*1.4, stance colour 2) matches android :3066-3076 (REVERSED_STANCE, base*1.5, colour 2), and web :3141-3154 (§1t12223s0§, flat base, floor 100, colour 3) matches android :3077-3090 (DUAL_STANCE, flat base, floor 100, colour 3). LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md has zero hits for '12223'. Consequence: the Focus drain is Balanced+REVERSED x1.0 and Heavy+DUAL x1.5 - the reverse of what cite-s27b/focus-meter-numerics-are-fully-recovered-in-web-v0717 states in prose.
